notes: No setup at all. One API call with the shared system prompt. Counted as the floor against which the other three are measured.

Enumerate tracked text files; order them by the documented relevance tiering; measure per-file tokens to find the budget boundary; concatenate. No account, no extra credential, no service. The token measurement is a measurement requirement, not a requirement of stuffing itself -- a user could concatenate until the API rejects the request.

Three local tool functions (grep/glob/read, ~135 lines) plus one system binary. One failed attempt, and it is the interesting part of the C1 story: `rg` answered at an interactive shell prompt but shutil.which('rg') returned None, because what answered was a shell function, not a binary. subprocess.run(['rg',...]) therefore raised FileNotFoundError. The arm was unrunnable for an entire implementation session and the verification step that was supposed to catch it (`rg --version`) was satisfied by the same shim. Fixed by `brew install ripgrep` (ripgrep 15.2.0) plus a shutil.which guard in make_agentic_tools that raises at construction time rather than mid-run. Zero accounts and zero credentials remains true; "zero setup" does not.

Provision a Zilliz Cloud cluster; obtain an OpenAI API key; run the pinned MCP server via npx; configure five environment variables; index the corpus (249s wall-clock for 2,825 files / 13,900 chunks); poll to completion; cross-check the chunk count in Milvus; wire the MCP tools into the agent loop. Two external accounts and three credentials, against zero for every other arm -- that gap is the substantive part of the C1 answer. FOUR failed attempts, and the point worth making on stage is that THREE OF THE FOUR WERE SILENT: (1) the plan's COLLECTION_NAME_PREFIX is ignored by claude-context 0.1.15 -- the real variable is CODE_CHUNKS_COLLECTION_NAME_OVERRIDE -- so collections land under an auto-generated hash and a multi-scope sweep cannot identify its own indexes; (2) get_indexing_status reported "fully indexed, 1100 files, 1100 chunks" 19 seconds in while the server log showed 330/2825 files, because it treats the mere existence of a cloud collection as proof of completion -- trusting it exited the script, killed the server mid-index, and left a collection holding 21%% of the repo that answers queries perfectly happily; (3) get_collection_stats reports row_count 0 for a freshly-indexed collection because stats lag unflushed segments, so the naive chunk count is zero; (4) background sync and a filesystem trigger watcher are both ON by default and would re-embed the corpus mid-benchmark. Only failure (4) is documented; the rest were found by cross-checking against a second source. A user who did not cross-check would have benchmarked a 21%%-indexed corpus and never known.
